neighbours.label: the linking word in a symbolism statement (associated with / symbol of / represents / stands for) that maps an emblem to what it means
fire: In many cultures the owl is associated with wisdom and patience.
The dove has long been a symbol of peace and hope.
In the painting, the white lily represents purity and innocence.
The oak tree is seen as a sign of strength and endurance.
For sailors, the anchor symbolises stability and safety.
In Chinese tradition, the color gold stands for wealth and fortune.
The lotus flower is associated with rebirth in Buddhist art.
The snake on the staff is an emblem of healing and medicine.
quiet: In many forests the owl is active at night and hunts mice.
The dove has long been kept by farmers for its meat and eggs.
In the painting, the white lily sits in a blue vase by the window.
The oak tree is grown in parks for its shade and timber.
For sailors, the anchor is lowered when the ship reaches harbour.
In Chinese markets, gold is sold by weight in small shops.
The lotus flower grows in shallow ponds across Asia.
The snake on the path was a harmless grass snake.

notes: Output direction of the + pole promotes 'symbol*'; the - pole is the symbol-meaning link itself.
